claim.pdf_says: "-  '-   literal continuation indicator   continuation of a literal when specified in an un-terminated literal with the same quotation symbol in its opening delimiter, subject to additional rules in 6.1.2.1, Syntax Rules.
claim.markdown_says:
| "- | literal continuation | continuation of a literal when specified in an un-terminated |
|---|---|---|
| '- | indicator | literal with the same quotation symbol in its opening delimiter, |

subject to additional rules in 6.1.2.1, Syntax Rules.
claim.why_it_matters: The floating-indicator table is broken up: '- is presented as a separate row whose indicator name is 'indicator' and whose meaning is a sentence fragment, instead of both "- and '- being literal continuation indicators with one shared description; the *> row's two numbered meanings and the >> and >>D rows also fall out of the table as loose paragraphs, losing the column association.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 45 (sheet 23), 6.1.2, shows one table with five entries. "- and '- are stacked in the Character-string column of a single entry, with the indicator name 'literal continuation indicator' and one three-line description. The markdown splits the visual lines of that entry into table rows. As a result the row for '- has the indicator name 'indicator' and a mid-sentence fragment as its meaning, and 'subject to additional rules in 6.1.2.1' falls outside the table. The *> entry is cut off after its first line (a table of one row, with the rest as loose paragraphs), and the >> and >>D entries are plain paragraphs that lose their column boundaries. Every word is present, so no normative text is missing. The fault is the table structure: read literally, the markdown gives '- the wrong name and description. That makes it a real structural defect, not only line wrapping.
verdict.corrected_description: Structural only, no text lost. The 6.1.2 floating-indicator table is transcribed by visual line, not by entry. The "- / '- entry is split into two rows, so '- appears with the name 'indicator' and a description fragment, and the description's last line drops out of the table. The *> entry's second line and item 2) fall out of the table as paragraphs, and the >> and >>D entries are untabled paragraphs. The fix is one table with five entries: *> (both numbered meanings), >>, "- and '- (one entry, 'literal continuation indicator'), and >>D.
